From fbb77611e95d3d5b2af86a59754a3130877cb667 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Dmitry V. Levin" <ldv@altlinux.org>
Date: Sat, 5 Aug 2017 23:00:50 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] Fix compat_sys_sigpending breakage

The latest change of compat_sys_sigpending in commit 8f13621abced
("sigpending(): move compat to native") has broken it in two ways.

First, it tries to write 4 bytes more than userspace expects:
sizeof(old_sigset_t) == sizeof(long) == 8 instead of
sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t) == sizeof(u32) == 4.

Second, on big endian architectures these bytes are being written in the
wrong order.

This bug was found by strace test suite.

Reported-by: Anatoly Pugachev <matorola@gmail.com>
Inspired-by: Eugene Syromyatnikov <evgsyr@gmail.com>
Fixes: 8f13621abced ("sigpending(): move compat to native")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry V. Levin <ldv@altlinux.org>
Acked-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/kernel/signal.c b/kernel/signal.c
index caed9133ae52..7e33f8c583e6 100644
--- a/kernel/signal.c
+++ b/kernel/signal.c
@@ -3303,12 +3303,15 @@ SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, old_sigset_t __user *, set)
 #ifdef CONFIG_COMPAT
 COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)
 {
+#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN
 	sigset_t set;
-	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)); 
-	if (err == 0)
-		if (copy_to_user(set32, &set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)))
-			err = -EFAULT;
+	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(set.sig[0]));
+	if (!err)
+		err = put_user(set.sig[0], set32);
 	return err;
+#else
+	return sys_rt_sigpending((sigset_t __user *)set32, sizeof(*set32));
+#endif
 }
 #endif
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `kernel/signal.c`**
   - The `sigpending` compatibility syscall (`COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)`) has been modified to address two main issues:
     - The size of the signal set being handled has been corrected. Instead of using `sizeof(old_sigset_t)`, which is 8 bytes, it now uses `sizeof(set.sig[0])`, which is 4 bytes, aligning with the expected size for `compat_old_sigset_t`.
     - The handling of big-endian architectures has been introduced. If the architecture is big-endian, the function now uses `put_user(set.sig[0], set32)` to correctly write the signal set to user space, ensuring the correct byte order is maintained.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes made in the `kernel/signal.c` file are directly related to fixing the issues introduced by a previous commit (8f13621abced) that moved the compatibility implementation of `sigpending` to a native implementation. The patch addresses the incorrect size and byte order issues that arose from this change, ensuring that the compatibility syscall behaves as expected in both little-endian and big-endian architectures. The modifications ensure that the data written to user space matches the expected format, thus resolving the breakage reported by the strace test suite.

Here is the commit message:
Fix compat_sys_sigpending breakage

The latest change of compat_sys_sigpending in commit 8f13621abced
("sigpending(): move compat to native") has broken it in two ways.

First, it tries to write 4 bytes more than userspace expects:
sizeof(old_sigset_t) == sizeof(long) == 8 instead of
sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t) == sizeof(u32) == 4.

Second, on big endian architectures these bytes are being written in the
wrong order.

This bug was found by strace test suite.

Reported-by: Anatoly Pugachev <matorola@gmail.com>
Inspired-by: Eugene Syromyatnikov <evgsyr@gmail.com>
Fixes: 8f13621abced ("sigpending(): move compat to native")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry V. Levin <ldv@altlinux.org>
Acked-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `compat_sys_sigpending` implementation writing 8 bytes instead of the expected 4 bytes to user space, due to using `sizeof(old_sigset_t)` instead of `sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t)`. Additionally, on big-endian architectures, the bytes were written in the wrong order, leading to incorrect data being passed to user space.

Here is the patch:
 COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)
 {
+#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN
 	sigset_t set;
-	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)); 
-	if (err == 0)
-		if (copy_to_user(set32, &set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)))
-			err = -EFAULT;
+	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(set.sig[0]));
+	if (!err)
+		err = put_user(set.sig[0], set32);
 	return err;
+#else
+	return sys_rt_sigpending((sigset_t __user *)set32, sizeof(*set32));
+#endif
 }
 #endif

The bug was caused by the `compat_sys_sigpending` implementation writing 8 bytes instead of the expected 4 bytes to user space, due to using `sizeof(old_sigset_t)` instead of `sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t)`. ```
Reason:
The implementation of `compat_sys_sigpending` incorrectly uses `sizeof(old_sigset_t)` (which is 8 bytes) instead of `sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t)` (which is 4 bytes), leading to writing more bytes than expected to user space. Additionally, on big-endian architectures, the order of the bytes written is incorrect.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(set.sig[0]));
err = put_user(set.sig[0], set32);
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the size used in `do_sigpending` to `sizeof(set.sig[0])`, which is 4 bytes, matching the expected size for `compat_old_sigset_t`. It also replaces `copy_to_user` with `put_user`, which is more appropriate for writing a single value, ensuring the correct data is passed to user space.
